shared_elements: low relief carved on tan/buff stone slab
band of repeated small units (row of short strokes/rectangles)
repeated chevron/zigzag or triangular fringe pattern
abstract sign-like shapes arranged in registers
justification: Both are buff-coloured stone surfaces in shallow relief that combine a bird seen in profile, a disc, and a repeated band of small evenly spaced units with a fringe of triangular/zigzag marks, which is the most specific correspondence. But A organises everything into strict symmetrical vertical columns around a central enclosed sign-group in crisp, ruled, sunk-line carving, whereas B has irregular, rounded, modelled animal bodies scattered freely across an unruled field under one horizontal register, so the compositional logic and the carving hand look quite unrelated.
